segments.text: This woman has exactly fourteen days to prove she can survive on her own. Bram is newly separated, her husband has moved on, and if she can't find a home for herself and her daughter Hollis fast, things with her ex are going to get ugly.
So she tours a giant four-story brownstone in Manhattan. The agents can't stop selling it: an elevator, endless rooms, and a price that seems too good to be true.
And there's a catch nobody mentions until later. The previous owner was a paranoid, reclusive millionaire, and half of his fortune has gone missing, so his heirs are now suing each other.

Then Bram notices that one corner of the master bedroom looks wrong. Behind it is a hidden panic room: steel walls, its own phone line, its own air supply, and a wall of monitors covering the entire house.
Bram, who is claustrophobic, hates it immediately. She also learns that the heavy steel door has a sensor that stops it from closing on anything in its way. Remember that.
On their first night, mother and daughter eat pizza on the floor and trade insults about the ex-husband and his new girlfriend. For a moment, it almost feels like a fresh start.
But that same night, three men break in. And they get the shock of their lives: the house was supposed to be empty, but a woman and a little girl are asleep upstairs.

One of them, Lena, wants out immediately. Robbing a house is one thing, but he refuses to do it with people inside. The planner, Rufus, insists the job will take forty-five minutes. And Rufus has brought a third man nobody else knows: Milo, who is carrying a gun.
Rufus finally reveals the prize: fourteen million dollars hidden upstairs, enough to wipe out Lena's debts forever. Lena stays.
Upstairs, Bram sees the intruders on the monitors. She grabs Hollis and they sprint for the panic room, slamming the door just before the men reach them.
They're safe. Except Bram never connected the panic room's phone, so they can't call anyone.
Inside, Bram nervously asks Hollis if she feels shaky or cold, a small question that will matter later.
Bram bluffs over the intercom that the police are on their way. Then the burglars hold up a message that changes everything: what they want is inside that room.
And here's the irony: Lena builds panic rooms for a living. He knows nobody can break in. So the plan becomes forcing the family out, and sealing the house so they can't escape once they do.
Locked in a tiny space, Bram starts having a panic attack, and it's her daughter who talks her down.
Then Rufus pumps gas into the room's vents. Lena protests that if the two pass out, they'll never get in, but Rufus doesn't care.
Bram flashes an SOS at a neighbor, who completely ignores it, while the burglars start fighting over how to split the money.
Meanwhile we learn that Rufus is actually the dead millionaire's grandson, robbing his own family. Milo threatens Lena, but Rufus reminds him they can't open the safe without Lena.
Bram takes a huge risk. She runs out of the room to grab her cell phone and makes it back just in time, only to discover it has no signal inside the steel walls.
So she splices into the house's main phone line and gets through to 911, and they put her on hold. Then the line goes dead.
They manage a garbled call to Hollis's father. Bram insists he'll come for them. But then Hollis admits what she has been hiding: she's dizzy and thirsty.
Hollis is diabetic, her blood sugar is crashing, and her emergency injection is in a fridge outside the panic room.

Out in the house, Rufus has had enough and tries to walk away. Big mistake. Milo stops him, apparently shooting him, and takes control of the operation, forcing Lena at gunpoint to find a way into the room.

Then Hollis's father finally arrives, and walks straight into the burglars' hands. They beat him in front of the cameras to make Bram open the door, and as Hollis screams for her dad, her body starts to give out.
Now the tables have turned. The burglars are inside the panic room with Hollis, and Bram is outside with the medicine, screaming that her daughter needs it.

Lena asks what happens if the girl doesn't get the shot. Coma. Death. So he gives her the injection himself, telling her about years of bad luck and gambling that cost him his house, his car and his wife. Milo just sneers that he's saved her for ten minutes.
Then the police show up, and Bram, knowing the men are holding her daughter, has to send them away with an embarrassing lie.
The safe is finally opened, and Milo makes his plan clear: no witnesses. Lena refuses.
In the chaotic final fight, Bram gets her hands on the gun and turns it on Milo. Lena grabs the money and runs, straight into police officers telling him to put his hands up.
Some time later, mother and daughter sit together browsing real-estate listings. They need a new home. Preferably one without a panic room.
